Round 1 returned REVISE on a gating HIGH from guardian, and the objection was correct: I scoped tokenURL/ConfirmTokenURL OUT of round 1 because handover.go belongs to the 477 lane and is mid-flight, and then in the same submission authored send_followup_email_action.go, which is equally theirs. That edit is REMOVED. Every other objection is answered below with a check I ran myself.
rationale:
WHAT IS WRONG, AND IT IS NOT THE SENTENCE.

bugs_open/475 is a FALSE STATEMENT TO A PAYING CUSTOMER. delivery-email-sender's live
body_template says "The ZIP comes with instructions that walk you through putting it on free
hosting." The ZIP contains 45 site files and no document of any kind. [MEASURED 2026-09-04 14:40Z]
at the live agent_definitions row - timestamped deliberately, because migration 776 was applied to
that SAME jsonb path at 12:05:25Z the same day for an unrelated false-promise clause, so "that
template was migrated today" is not evidence either way. The bugs_open/477 lane independently
confirmed the clause with a LIKE predicate. Two lanes, two instruments, same answer.

The point fix is obvious and I am NOT proposing it: add {{instructions_link}} to fillTemplate and a
fifth line to each of the two guard slices. I am not proposing it because it GROWS the structure
that is the actual defect.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT: TWO CUSTOMER LETTERS, ONE VOCABULARY, TWO HAND-KEPT MIRRORS.

send_delivery_email_action.go fills its template through fillTemplate (:197-206), a
strings.NewReplacer over a CLOSED vocabulary of seven tokens. It guards with a hand-written slice
(:125-134) that must run BEFORE delivery.Claim stamps the handover - because a named token with no
value is replaced by an EMPTY STRING, so the customer reads "Your files: " with nothing after it,
and NO POST-FILL SCAN CAN SEE THAT, because the fill succeeded. The post-fill "{{" backstop
(:168-175) fires AFTER the stamp, which is worse.

send_followup_email_action.go - a SECOND customer letter, built by the 477 lane, seeded disabled by
migration 775 - CALLS THE SAME fillTemplate (:224) and keeps its OWN MIRRORED guard slice
(:166-172).

The contract holding those two lists in step is A COMMENT, in that file, at :150-164:

  "The only other placeholder-refusal in the estate is send_delivery_email's, which this copies
   deliberately rather than shares. ... If a shared mechanism is ever built, these two are its
   first two callers."
  "If fillTemplate's vocabulary grows, this list must grow with it."

OWNER RULING 2026-08-02 s2 (RFC_010) already ruled on exactly this shape: "A comment is not a
control on a tree this many sessions share."

AND THE ESTATE DEMONSTRATED IT THIS AFTERNOON, LIVE, NOT HYPOTHETICALLY. Two sessions, both
careful, both correct, independently chose TWO NAMES FOR ONE CONCEPT for the new instructions
placeholder: this lane's {{instructions_link}} and the 477 lane's {{instructions_url}}. What caught
it was one lane having written that comment and the other thinking to send a cross-session message.
NEITHER IS A MECHANISM. Half a day's difference in timing and the estate would carry two
differently-named placeholders for one page, filled by two different mechanisms, in two letters to
the same customer.

WHAT THIS CHANGE DOES.

Single-source the vocabulary and DERIVE both guards from it, so "the filler knows a token the guard
does not" becomes UNREPRESENTABLE rather than discouraged. A sender declares an Availability for
every token; Fill.Check refuses on COVERAGE (a token nobody declared) before it refuses on
AVAILABILITY (a token the template names with no value). Coverage is checked unconditionally, not
only when a template happens to name the token, so adding a token to the Vocabulary makes every
sender that has not been taught refuse LOUDLY and PRE-STAMP - recoverable - instead of mailing an
empty string. {{instructions_link}} then lands as the first single-sourced entry rather than the
last hand-copied one.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, stated so no seat has to ask.

It checks PLACEHOLDERS. It cannot check PROSE. "The ZIP comes with instructions" carries no
placeholder and was invisible to the existing guard; it will be invisible to this one. The change
NARROWS the class by making the customer-facing artefact a link, and links are checked. It does not
eliminate it. A generic "false English claim" detector was considered and rejected (see edit 5's
rationale).

WHY THIS IS COUNCIL-SCOPE AND NOT AN RFC. Under OWNER RULING 2026-07-29 s1, a shared-vocabulary
addition needs an RFC only when it changes what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES. This one
STRENGTHENS the guarantee (from "a comment asks you to keep two lists in step" to "an undeclared
token refuses before the stamp") and adds NO new authority - so RFC_022's narrowing does not bite
either: there is no new opt-in field whose unsafe default is OFF. If the architecture seat reads it
otherwise I would rather hear that now.

ORDERING, WHICH IS A LIVE FAILURE MODE AND NOT A PREFERENCE. Config is live on apply; Go is inert
until a roll. A template naming {{instructions_link}} before the binary knows it leaves the literal
in the body, trips the post-fill "{{" scan - and that scan fires AFTER the handover is stamped. The
result is a stamped, undeliverable handover needing the operator re-mint recipe. So NO MIGRATION IS
IN THIS ROUND. The template change comes only after this code has rolled, verified by
service_binary_capabilities plus git merge-base --is-ancestor.

The owner has separately ruled NO interim copy change ("leave it") until the instructions page
exists, so there is no competing change queued against that jsonb path.

NEW IN ROUND 2, AND IT CLOSES A LANDMINE FILED TODAY. The pre-claim guard validates the VALUES of

THE POST-FILL "{{" SCAN STAYS, and the sketch says why so nobody deletes it as redundant: coverage
asks "does the vocabulary know this token?", the post-fill scan asks "did Apply actually substitute
it?" - a declared token that passes Check and still survives the fill is invisible to coverage by
construction, and it is the one that puts literal mustache in a customer's inbox.
